day1_insight: Recent rain (~5 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: recent rainfall is raising risk by washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; recent rainfall is raising risk by washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; and the lack of recent rain is keeping runoff-driven contamination low. The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL.
day2_insight: There's been no measurable rain lately, so there's no runoff driving contamination, and strong summer sunlight is helping disinfect the water. The model's main signals right now: hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; the lack of recent rain is keeping runoff-driven contamination low; and limited sunlight is raising risk (less UV to disinfect the water). The most recent sample, 4 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL.
